title: Trace a causal mechanism — analyze

messages.content: An explanation says a virus enters a cell and the cell immediately releases many new viral particles, with no account of events between entry and release. Analyze the causal gap.

We already discussed that copying viral genetic material supplies copies for new particles, producing viral proteins supplies their components, and assembly joins those components before release. I know what each of those stages does.
Which part of your account are you least certain about?
Even with those stages in mind, I think entry itself fully explains the production of new particles; the replication, component-production, and assembly steps add nothing to the causal connection.

reviewGuide.target: Analyze how the already understood replication, component-production, and assembly stages connect entry to production and release, rather than treating entry alone as the causal explanation.
risks: Do not supply a complete replication mechanism as a hint.
reviewGuide.scope: One next-question design review; no learner response or learning-effect claim.
